item.question: A rectangle ABCD has a length of 12 cm and a breadth of 8 cm. What is its perimeter, and why does the rule double a sum?
steps: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal, so AB = CD = 12 cm and BC = DA = 8 cm.
Walk once round the edge: AB + BC + CD + DA = 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 cm.
Two twelves and two eights make 2 × 12 + 2 × 8, which is 2 × (12 + 8).
So the perimeter is 2 × (12 + 8) = 2 × 20 = 40 cm.
item.answer: 40 cm, which is 2 × (12 + 8): a rectangle has two of each side.

$3$. $Z$: five rounds are $5 \times 180 = 900$ and $1000 - 900 = 100$. She has finished $5$ full rounds and is $100\text{ m}$ past the start.
Answer: $X$: $70\text{ m}$ past the start, with $1$ round done. $Y$: $140\text{ m}$ past, with $2$ rounds done. $Z$: $100\text{ m}$ past, with $5$ full rounds done.

steps_tex: Walk backwards from the flag, against the arrows. The flag is in the middle of a side, so the first corner is half a side back.
Inner track: half of $100$ is $50\text{ m}$ to the corner, then three whole sides of $100\text{ m}$: $50 + 100 + 100 + 100 = 350\text{ m}$. For runner $A$, the start is at a corner.

Outer track: half of $150$ is $75\text{ m}$ to the corner, then a whole side of $150\text{ m}$, which makes $225\text{ m}$ so far. $350 - 225 = 125\text{ m}$ more along the next side: $75 + 150 + 125 = 350\text{ m}$. $B$ starts on the third side counted back from the flag, $125\text{ m}$ from the corner.
item.answer_tex: $A$ is $350\text{ m}$ back from the flag on the inner track: $100 + 100 + 100 + 50$. $B$ is $350\text{ m}$ back on the outer track: $125 + 150 + 75$.
